subject: Dedicated fleet SLO alignment & traffic clarifications
messages:
From: Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@astrahealth.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Menon <ravi.menon@astrahealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial telemetry + questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We pulled a sample of production telemetry (attached) and sketched a first-pass SLA target: 95th latency <= 300ms for transactional prompts, and burst support for 20k concurrent interactive sessions during peak marketing campaigns.

Before we hand this to procurement, our VP of Engineering (Ravi) wants two clarifications that will determine whether we commit to a reserved pool or a hybrid approach:

1) How do you map prompt/response length distributions to GPU slot sizing? Our workload includes short transactional prompts (~15 tokens avg) and occasional long-context summarizations (~6k tokens).
2) When you say "burst support," how is burst capacity gated — is it pre-warmed slots, on-demand elasticity, or asynchronous queueing that impacts p99 tail?

Attached: astra_telemetry_sample_q2.csv (CSV), prompt_mix_snapshot.md (MD)

Can your sizing team sketch a conservative fleet footprint (GPU count + expected occupancy) and an approach to preserve our 95th latency during the 3-day marketing spikes?

Appreciate a short reply with next steps.

Thanks,
Aisha
Head of Product, AstraHealth

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@astrahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial telemetry + questions

Hi Aisha,

Thanks — we got the sample. Looping in Marissa (pre-sales sizing lead) and Ben (runtime architect) to give you a concise footprint and an ops plan. Quick answers up-front, then we'll follow with a short sizing doc: 

- Prompt/response mapping: we don't size purely on average token counts — we target the tail of the prompt length distribution and the dominant latency SLO. Short transactional prompts can be packed with higher concurrency on a smaller GPU instance class; long-context jobs (6k tokens) are treated as session-affine and often pinned to larger instances or run on quantized variants with KV-cache persistence to avoid repeated warmups.

- Burst gating: three levers — preallocated reserved slots (fastest), elastic burst from pooled capacity (near-instant but dependent on free capacity), and staged queueing with graceful degradation (accepts requests and serves lower-cost model variants or higher-latency fallback). Our recommendation typically mixes reserved slots for baseline and burst pool with automatic prioritization for critical routes.

Action items: Marissa will produce a conservative GPU-count sketch and a burst-runbook. Ben, can you add a short note on KV cache warm-start and how that affects the cost / p95 during sustained 3-day peaks?

Sooj
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@astrahealth.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial telemetry + questions

Aisha — good sample, thanks. I ran a quick pass with conservative assumptions and sketched three options (attached mini-workbook):

Option A (Conservative reserved): 24 x A100-80GB equivalent slots; targets steady-state occupancy 65%, reserve 40% of peak burst in warm pool. Expected token cost per 1M tokens: $X (internal est).

Option B (Hybrid reserved + burst): 12 reserved slots + 20 burst-capable slots (autoscale up to 32 during peaks). Warm pool kept at 20% of max burst; autoscale uses pre-warmed images for fastest provisioning on our Dedicated fabric.

Option C (Minimal reserve + fallback): 6 reserved slots; heavy reliance on on-demand pooled capacity and model-fallback routing. Lower committed cost but higher p95 risk during simultaneous long-context runs.

Notes & assumptions (brief):
- Transactional prompts: median request 15 tokens, tail to 120 tokens (2%); we assumed 150ms per-token compute for the transactional model on A100-80GB equivalent when batched.
- Long context sessions: we modeled average 6k token context with KV-cache persistence; these sessions reduce effective concurrency by a factor of ~6 compared to transactional calls because KV cache increases memory per-session.
- Warm-start: we assume a 60s cold-to-warm warmup for an isolated variant; KV cache persistence and sticky routing reduce repeated warmup for returning sessions.

Attached for your review: astra_dedicated_mini_workbook.xlsx (XLSX) — I'll export a lightweight summary next.

Propose a 30-min call today to walk the options and pick an initial commitment tier. I'm free 14:00-16:00 PT.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Pre-Sales Sizing Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aisha Khanna <aisha.k@astrahealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial telemetry + questions

Aisha / team — a couple of technical clarifications to make the footprint tighter: 

1) Session affinity & KV cache: If Astra can accept a 5-minute session affinity window (sticky routing), we can amortize KV cache across repeat interactions and recover ~30-40% effective concurrency on the same hardware compared to fully stateless runs.

2) Background maintenance & checkpointing: schedule regular model weights load windows during low-traffic hours (we suggest 02:00-04:00 local) to keep warm pools healthy; this reduces cold starts during bursts.

3) Canary routing during peaks: implement a small canary route that runs high-priority traffic on reserved nodes and routes best-effort traffic to the burst pool — keeps p95 under control without doubling reserved capacity.

I'll draft a one-page operational playbook around these points and attach it to Marissa's workbook.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Runtime Architect, Redwood Inference

• Can you confirm whether the warm-pool reservation can be scoped to region (we want US-only)?

Let's take Marissa's 30-min slot at 15:00 PT today to finalize numbers. We'll have our procurement lead (cc'd on the calendar invite) on the call for commitment guidance.

Ravi
